reason: Verified by driving the master, not inferred. owner-editing at 390x844 loads with the edited .b-copy at top 996 in a 844px viewport - 152px below the fold - while .b-edit is position:fixed spanning 464-832 (368px, 43.6% of the viewport); same shape at 768x1024 (row 1056, sheet 667-1012) and 1024x900 (row 1016, sheet 543-888). grep of b.css finds no padding-bottom and no [data-editor-open] rule anywhere, so the attribute openEditor sets is never used and no band is reserved: the claim that nothing scrolls it into view is correct. The keyboard half is also correct as stated - after Enter on a .b-grab, document.activeElement is still .b-grab, .b-editHost precedes .b-measure in DOM order (compareDocumentPosition confirms), and from the last row the forward Tab leaves the document (activeElement becomes BODY) before re-entering at the header acts. One sub-claim is overstated and should not be carried into the fix: tapping a row in owner-flight is NOT occluded 'every time'. Focusing the grab already scrolls it into view, so at 390 rows 0-5 land at 363-436, clear above the 464-832 sheet; only row 6 lands inside it (485-558), and at 768 only rows 0 and 6 are occluded. The defect is real at the entry state and at the edge rows, not universally. It survives the gates because interaction-check.mjs never asserts that the edited row is visible - only that the readout, count, date and focus track the move.
sharpenedFix:
The fix aims right but is wrong in three places; land it as follows.

1. RECONCILE WITH THE ROUND-1 GATE. interaction-check.mjs:346-366 opens owner-editing at 1440x960, presses -7 once, and asserts both 'the page keeps its place through the move' (scrollY unchanged) and 'the steppers do not move under the pointer' (identical .b-step client rects). Measured: at 1440 the row goes 657 -> 624, so the proposed guard evaluates false and scrollY stays 0 - the assertion passes today, but only by accident. It stops being an accident later in the same test: after the 20 forward presses the row sits at 1665 and the guard flips true. And a desktop scroll is genuinely destructive there, because .b-stick is position:sticky and not yet stuck at scrollY 0 - I measured a 300px scrollBy dragging every .b-step 167px up the viewport, which is exactly the 'button you were about to press again moved out from under the cursor' regression the openEditor comment says was already paid for once. So do NOT call the scroll on every setAway. Gate it on the sheet: at the top of setAway compute var panel = root.querySelector('.b-edit'); var fixed = panel && getComputedStyle(panel).position === 'fixed'; and run the scroll only when fixed is true. Where the editor is fixed (<=1024) the steppers live inside the viewport-anchored sheet and cannot move under the finger; where it is static (1280/1440) the scroll path is now unreachable, so both gate assertions hold by construction rather than by luck. Then add one assertion of your own at 390x844 - after a stepper press the edited .b-copy is fully inside [16, sheetTop-16] - so the new behaviour is guarded too.

2. SCROLLING ALONE CANNOT FIX THE LAST ROWS. At 390 the occluded row 6 is reached at scrollY 1519, which is exactly docHeight 2363 minus viewport 844: the page is already at maximum scroll, so window.scrollBy is clamped to zero and the row stays under the sheet no matter what the guard computes. Reserve the band in layout first: while root has [data-editor-open] and the sheet is fixed, add padding-bottom to the scrolling column equal to the sheet's height plus 24px (read it once from .b-edit's offsetHeight into a --b-sheet custom property on open, clear it in closeEditor). Only with that headroom does the scroll in openEditor/setAway have anywhere to go.

3. FOCUS THE PANEL, NOT THE TITLE FIELD. Moving focus into the panel is right - the panel is upstream of the measure so the tab loop is currently broken - but do not focus #b-edit-title. On a phone that raises the software keyboard, which resizes the visual viewport and re-lays the fixed sheet you just scrolled against, and the sibling finding editor-title-field-discards-what-is-typed shows that field currently commits nothing, so it is the worst possible landing point. Give .b-edit tabindex="-1" plus role="group" and an aria-label naming the moment being edited, and focus the panel element itself. Escape and Done already return focus to the .b-grab (render-b.js:452-466), so the loop closes without touching them.
